text: When an ECP5 FIR is DSP-capped at 12>8 while timing has margin (235.7 MHz, 4.24 ns carry-chain accumulator), do not apply symmetric fold=2 with dsp_regs=in_pipe_out without checking the pre-multiplier path: it reaches 8 DSP but Fmax falls to 100.7 MHz because the 2:1 operand mux/coefficient ROM makes FF part[1] -> LUT4 out_data -> carry-chain the 9.93 ns critical path.

When an ECP5 folded symmetric FIR meets its 8-DSP cap at fold=2 but is timing-limited by the post-multiplier gather into a 36-cell carry chain over 4.33 ns of route, insert two fabric pipeline stages after the multiplier (pipe_mul 0→2) to split the accumulation path, gaining +11.2 MHz (100.7→111.9 MHz) for +2 LUT and 0 DSP.

When an ECP5 symmetric-folded FIR with 8 DSPs is timing-limited at 111.9 MHz by a fabric path of part[0] FF → 6-LUT4 out_data tree → 34-cell carry chain, avoid changing acc_width 40→38, pipe_mul 2→3, and reg_in false→true: it cut LUTs by 43 but dropped Fmax 6.4 MHz to 105.5 MHz with no DSP savings and remained infeasible because the accumulator/fabric sum, not the multiplier pipeline, dominates.

When a symmetric folded FIR on ECP5 is timing-limited by routing through the tap-operand mux/coefficient ROM (critical path FF -> 5-cell LUT4 (~4.2 ns route) -> 33-cell carry chain, no DSP), increase fold from 2 to 4 (halving DSPs from 8 to 4) to relieve pre-multiplier congestion, which shortens the carry chain to 9 cells and raises Fmax by 24.3 MHz (105.5 to 129.8 MHz) while cutting 457 LUTs.

When the ECP5 4-fold symmetric FIR hits 129.8 MHz on the 17-bit pre-adder carry chain (2.29 ns) into the MULT18X18D A input, de-share the coefficients and double fold to 8 to keep 4 MACs/4 DSPs and cut the pre-adder, but the replacement 3-level 8:1 operand mux becomes critical, so LUTs fall 137 while Fmax drops 3.5 MHz to 126.3 MHz—fix the mux or leave the pre-adder.
